grader: format-neutral gpt-4o LLM-judge, applied identically to all three arches

keyword_grader_reference.note: under the keyword grader (G-07), SQL retrieval was 11.1% — the delta below is how much of that was format artifact

corrects_g07: G-07 attributed SQL's low retrieval score mainly to a grading format artifact. The format-neutral judge shows that was mostly wrong: SQL stays at 11.1% on retrieval even when format is credited neutrally — raw text-to-SQL genuinely underperforms on these scenarios. The format artifact was concentrated in the generative scenarios (e.g. the 'ML recipe' id 116) that are excluded from this retrieval subset.
grader_leniency_finding: Every tier collapses vs the keyword grader (graph 81.0%->37.0%, docs 66.7%->25.9%). Spot-check shows why: the graph/doc tiers pass many keyword-grader scenarios with fluent prose that ECHOES the expected entity names but contains no actual answer (e.g. ids 10/11/42 return prose about Chiller 6/Tonnage with zero values, because the sensor time-series isn't in the graph). A format-neutral judge correctly fails those. So the AssetOpsBench-style keyword grader materially INFLATES scores via prose-echo leniency.
verdict: Format-neutral, retrieval-only: documents 25.9% / graph 37.0% / SQL 11.1%. The graph advantage is REAL even neutral (+11.1pp over documents, +25.9pp over SQL), but far smaller in absolute terms than the keyword-grader headline suggested — most of the graph tier's 81% was grader leniency, and raw SQL genuinely trails on retrieval (not merely a format artifact).
